newsitem.title: USA: Westinghouse, Infinity shareholders vote on merger.
newsitem.headline: Westinghouse, Infinity shareholders vote on merger.

text.p: Shareholders of Westinghouse Electric Corp. and Infinity Broadcasting Corp. voted Tuesday on steps that help pave the way for completion of the companies' $3.9 billion merger.

Westinghouse said its shareholders voted by an "overwhelming majority" to raise the number of the company's shares outstanding to complete the stock swap merger with Infinity, the nation's No. 2 radio broadcaster behind Pittsburgh-based Westinghouse.
Separately, Infinity shareholders voted to approve the deal, which was announced on June 20 and still needs approval from the Federal Communications Commission.
The Justice Department approved the deal on Nov. 12, after Westinghouse and Infinity agreed to sell stations in Chicago and Dallas to comply with local station ownership limits.
The combined radio group will operate 79 stations in 17 markets, including 64 stations in the top 10 markets.
